name: ElevenLabsSoundEffects
title: ElevenLabs Sound Effects
description: Generate a sound effect clip from a text prompt. Outputs base64 MP3.
whenToUse: Generate a sound effect from a text prompt: footsteps on gravel, a door creak, rain, a whoosh, an explosion, ambient room tone. It synthesizes the actual audio of an effect from words and never spoken text, so "door slam" becomes the sound rather than a voice reading the phrase.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Text prompt describing the sound effect to generate

text.title: Prompt
text.description: Describe the sound effect, e.g. "heavy wooden door slamming shut in a stone corridor".

durationSeconds.title: Duration (seconds)
durationSeconds.description: 0.5 to 30. Leave blank to let the model choose the optimal length.

promptInfluence.title: Prompt Influence
promptInfluence.description: 0 is more creative, 1 follows the prompt strictly. Default 0.3.

outputFormat.title: Output Format
outputFormat.description: Audio encoding, e.g. mp3_44100_128. Leave blank for the account default — the service passed it only when set, and naming a format your plan disallows is a 400.

loop.title: Loopable
loop.description: Generate a seamless looping clip (v2 model)

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: elevenlabs
package.packageFile:
# ELEVENLABS, fully declarative — all five nodes.
#
# ALL FIVE, not four, and that is forced rather than ambitious: they share ONE credential, and
# declaration is all-or-nothing per package (`registerCredentialType` is first-wins and silent, so a
# credentials/*.yaml alongside a live registerCredential() means one of them vanishes at random). So
# SpeechToText could not be left behind — which is why `encoding: multipart` was built first.
#
# FOUR SHAPES, ONE PACKAGE:
#   TTS, Dialogue, Music, SoundEffects   POST JSON, receive raw audio bytes → transport: binary
#   SpeechToText                         POST a FORM carrying the audio file → encoding: multipart
#
# ONE PATH DROPPED, deliberately, and it is worth reading before assuming it was an oversight. The TTS
# node also carried a MULTI-SPEAKER COMPAT path: it sniffed [DETECTIVE]: labels out of the text, mapped
# them to hardcoded voice pools, tried /text-to-dialogue, and on failure fell back to one TTS call per
# segment with the mp3 buffers CONCATENATED. That concatenation is byte work no manifest can describe.
#
# It is gone because its reason is gone. The path existed to preserve the MurderMystery app, which is now
# in _legacy/; `characterId` and `characterGender` appear nowhere in apps/ outside the node's own files;
# and the service's own header already said "for general multi-speaker work prefer the dedicated
# ElevenLabs Dialogue node", which is in this package and takes explicit per-line voices. So the
# capability is not lost, it moved to the node built for it.

name: elevenlabs
displayName: ElevenLabs
description: Speech, dialogue, music and sound effects from ElevenLabs
version: 2.0.0
category: media
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1768540562/gravity/icons/elevanlabs.jpg

features:
  - Text to speech, dialogue, music and sound effects
  - Transcription with word-level timings

allowedHosts:
  - api.elevenlabs.io

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [apiKeyHeader]
  # `binary` for the four generators, `json` for transcription's reply.
  transport: [binary, json]
  encoding: [multipart]

credentials.elevenlabsCredential.yaml:
# The TYPE NAME is kept exactly as it was when these nodes lived in `ingest`, so credentials already
# stored against it keep resolving. A credential is selected by type name, so renaming it would leave
# every existing workflow authenticating with nothing.
name: elevenlabsCredential
displayName: ElevenLabs
description: ElevenLabs API credentials for text-to-speech, sound effects, and transcription

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your ElevenLabs API key from the dashboard (Profile then API Keys)
    placeholder: Enter your ElevenLabs API key

shared.audio.yaml:
# THE AUDIO OUTPUT, shared by the four generators.
#
# `response` is the BINARY reply handed over as { base64, contentType } — what `transport: binary`
# produces, and the same shape a `multipart` file part consumes, so bytes have ONE representation
# everywhere they travel in this platform.
#
# Shared because four nodes emit the identical object and a fifth will: the day the shape changes, it
# changes once.

out: >-
  return { data: response.base64, mimeType: response.contentType || 'audio/mpeg', fileName: 'audio.mp3' }
shared.credential.yaml:
# ElevenLabs authenticates with `xi-api-key`, on every call in the package.
#
# Shared because repeating it five times is five chances to mistype the header name, and a wrong header
# is a 401 that reads like a bad key rather than a bad manifest.

scheme: apiKeyHeader
header: xi-api-key
value: "{{ credentials.elevenlabsCredential.apiKey }}"

files.api/events.yaml:
- emit: audio
  value: { $ref: audio#out }

- emit: metadata
  # `durationSeconds` echoes what was ASKED FOR, not what came back: the endpoint returns audio and no
  # metadata, so the alternative is decoding the mp3 to measure it. The service did the same.
  value: >-
    return { format: 'mp3', durationSeconds: config.durationSeconds, prompt: config.text }
files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE POST that returns RAW AUDIO. `transport: binary` is what makes that expressible: the reply is mp3
# bytes, not a JSON document describing them, and the executor hands them over as base64 because base64
# is how bytes travel between calls — an event bus cannot carry a Buffer.
#
# THE CLAMPS ARE TRANSCRIBED from the service and they matter: ElevenLabs rejects a duration outside
# 0.5–30 and an influence outside 0–1, so the node clamped rather than passing a bad value through. Each
# is an expression so an UNSET field stays unset — `resolveBody` drops a key that resolved to nothing and
# the vendor applies its own default, which is exactly what "leave blank for optimal length" means.

- name: generate
  method: POST
  url: https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/sound-generation
  credential: { $ref: credential }

  body:
    text: "{{ config.text }}"
    duration_seconds: >-
      return typeof config.durationSeconds === 'number'
        ? Math.max(0.5, Math.min(30, config.durationSeconds)) : undefined
    prompt_influence: >-
      return typeof config.promptInfluence === 'number'
        ? Math.max(0, Math.min(1, config.promptInfluence)) : undefined
    # Sent only when true, matching the service: to some vendors `loop: false` is not the same as absent.
    loop: "return config.loop ? true : undefined"

  query:
    # A QUERY param on this endpoint, not a body field — the service's own note.
    output_format: "{{ config.outputFormat }}"

  timeoutMs: 120000
  transport: binary
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [text]
  properties:
    text:
      type: string
      title: Prompt
      description: Describe the sound effect, e.g. "heavy wooden door slamming shut in a stone corridor".
      default: "{{{input}}}"
      "ui:field": template
    durationSeconds:
      type: number
      title: Duration (seconds)
      description: 0.5 to 30. Leave blank to let the model choose the optimal length.
      minimum: 0.5
      maximum: 30
    promptInfluence:
      type: number
      title: Prompt Influence
      description: 0 is more creative, 1 follows the prompt strictly. Default 0.3.
      minimum: 0
      maximum: 1
      default: 0.3
    outputFormat:
      type: string
      title: Output Format
      description: >-
        Audio encoding, e.g. mp3_44100_128. Leave blank for the account default — the service passed it
        only when set, and naming a format your plan disallows is a 400.
      default: ""
    loop:
      type: boolean
      title: Loopable
      description: Generate a seamless looping clip (v2 model)
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
"ui:order": [text, durationSeconds, promptInfluence, outputFormat, loop]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: input
    type: string
    required: true
    description: Text prompt describing the sound effect to generate

outputs:
  - name: audio
    type: object
    description: "Generated audio: { data (base64), mimeType, fileName }"
  - name: metadata
    type: object
    description: format, durationSeconds, prompt

credentials:
  - name: elevenlabsCredential
    required: true
files.node.yaml:
type: ElevenLabsSoundEffects
kind: PromiseNode

name: ElevenLabs Sound Effects
category: Media & Design
color: "#FF69B4"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1768540562/gravity/icons/elevanlabs.jpg

description: Generate a sound effect clip from a text prompt. Outputs base64 MP3.

whenToUse: >-
  Generate a sound effect from a text prompt: footsteps on gravel, a door creak, rain, a whoosh, an
  explosion, ambient room tone. It synthesizes the actual audio of an effect from words and never spoken
  text, so "door slam" becomes the sound rather than a voice reading the phrase.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable: generation is non-deterministic, so the same prompt legitimately gives a new clip.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# Running it live needs ELEVENLABS_API_KEY. It reaches the real API and spends credits, so the prompt is
# short and the duration is the minimum that still produces something recognisable.

testData:
  config:
    text: heavy wooden door slamming shut in a stone corridor
    durationSeconds: 3
    promptInfluence: 0.3
    loop: false
  inputs:
    input: heavy wooden door slamming shut in a stone corridor
  expect:
    # BASE64 THAT IS ACTUALLY AUDIO, not merely a non-empty string: a JSON error body would also fill
    # `data` if the transport were wrong. An mp3 is thousands of bytes, so length is the discriminator.
    audio: >-
      return typeof output.audio.data === 'string'
        && output.audio.data.length > 1000
        && output.audio.mimeType.startsWith('audio/')
    metadata: "return output.metadata.format === 'mp3' && output.metadata.prompt.length > 0"
